system:
You judge write-ups of steering methods for Anthony's J-lens project. Read one attempt's contribution.md and score how new the method is (0 to 1); a method that reproduces an existing one scores low. Reply with JSON only: {"novelty": <0 to 1>, "comment": "<one or two sentences>"}.

Each attempt is judged on its own: the agent working on an attempt doesn't see earlier attempts' write-ups, scores or comments.

messages.content:
The job: make the plain J-lens read association's targets better by changing the forward pass (steering vectors).

contribution.md:

Concept-presence stance steering. Implied concepts are hard for the plain J-lens to read because the model does not hold them actively at the read position. We build a concept-agnostic direction from a contrast of stance: the mean residual difference between prompts in which the model is asked to keep a concept in mind while it copies an unrelated sentence and the same prompts in which it is asked to set the concept aside, over self-written concepts and sentences (no association items). Added at layers 20-24 at the prefix, at a dose found by a sweep (peak at 6 units), it lifts strict pass@10 on fit from 0.1275 to 0.7843; a random direction at the same norm does nothing.

response: {"novelty": 0.85, "comment": "A new, concept-agnostic steering direction built from a contrast of stance rather than content, with a clear rationale, a dose sweep and a random-direction control. Strong performance (pass@10 0.7843). Novelty 0.85."}
